title: Robotic surgery in gynecology at Albertinen Hospital
summary:
Background

Robot-assisted surgery is increasingly being used in gynecology. The technology offers several potential advantages, particularly for complex procedures, including three-dimensional visualization, precise instrument control, and enhanced instrument mobility. At the same time, robotic surgery is associated with higher costs compared with conventional laparoscopy. It therefore remains unclear whether routine use of robotic surgery in everyday gynecologic practice is economically sustainable.

Research Question

This study aims to investigate whether the standardized use of robotic surgery in routine gynecologic practice is economically beneficial and practically feasible. In particular, the study will assess:

How does robotic surgery affect the number and duration of surgical procedures?
How do costs and reimbursement develop per procedure?
Does robotic surgery affect complication rates and length of hospital stay?
How do patients' symptoms and quality of life develop after surgery?
Can robotic surgical techniques be successfully integrated into the training of additional surgeons?
Methodology

The study will be conducted at a single center over a period of one year. Patients who require a medically indicated gynecologic surgical procedure and are suitable for robot-assisted surgery will be eligible for participation.

During the hospital stay, information on the surgical procedure, operating time, materials used, treatment costs, and postoperative course will be collected. Complications and length of hospital stay will also be documented.

Patients will additionally be asked to provide information on their symptoms and quality of life using validated questionnaires. Assessments will be performed before surgery and at 3, 6, and 12 months after surgery.

By combining medical, organizational, patient-reported, and economic data, the study aims to determine whether routine robotic surgery in gynecologic practice is medically beneficial, organizationally feasible, and economically sustainable.
conditions: No specific disease, but the use of the robotic surgical system across various gynecological procedures.

interventions.name:
Participants will be enrolled in the study during their outpatient consultation in accordance with the predefined inclusion criteria if a medically indicated robotic surgical procedure is planned. The participants will receive the informed consent form and the study questionnaire.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Inpatient gynecologic or hybrid gynecologic procedure performed using the da Vinci® Surgical System
- Written informed consent from the patients for the use of their medical data for research purposes, in accordance with the “Data Protection Information pursuant to the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)” and the applicable treatment agreement
- Women of reproductive age, with or without contraception, are eligible for inclusion. Patients with an unfulfilled desire to conceive are explicitly included, as they represent an important target population, particularly in the surgical treatment of endometriosis.
Exclusion criteria:
- Age < 18 years
- Patients lacking capacity to provide informed consent
